standard_prerequisites.name: 2-intersecting family of perfect matchings
standard_prerequisites.statement: A family of perfect matchings such that any two of its members share at least two pairs.
standard_prerequisites.use: Its characteristic function is the object of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Certificate of a matching
standard_prerequisites.statement: The set of pairs common to the members of the family, used to name them.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the sets whose intersection is prescribed.

standard_prerequisites.name: Size bound
standard_prerequisites.statement: The common certificate size is at most n minus two, so at least four indices remain free.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what makes the explicit pairing possible.

core_obligations: Aim again at the stronger statement: build a matching with the first certificate whose intersection with the second certificate is exactly the intersection of the two (source line 479).

List the pairs of the first certificate, take the indices not mentioned there and pair them in a fixed shifted manner, so that the new pairs avoid the second certificate because at least two shifted partners separate them (source lines 481-485).

proof_roadmap.step: Set up the stronger statement and collect the free indices.
Pair the free indices with a shift and check the avoidance.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 475-477, the matching analogue of the permutation result: for a 2-intersecting family of perfect matchings whose common certificate size is at most n minus two, two members with equal characteristic value admit representatives whose certificates meet exactly in the intersection of the original certificates. The proof (source lines 478-486) writes down the representative explicitly: it lists the pairs of the first certificate, collects the indices left free, and pairs them with a fixed shift, the shifted partner of an index being separated from it by at least the two pairs that the size bound leaves free, so that the new pairs cannot meet the second certificate. The statement records the existence of the representatives and neither the listing nor the shift argument.
